Behind the motion.

A mechanical sculpture inspired by watch movements and robotics, with scenes that connect to my projects. The models and choreography were built for this site. The interaction layer draws on these public examples and libraries.

References

  • Lusion — the visual reference for a generous editorial layout, glossy sculptural objects, and motion that drives the page.
  • Lusion’s WebGL Scroll Sync — DOM-aligned WebGL windows and an adapted five-sample, scroll-responsive displacement shader. MIT notice.
  • 14islands’ viewport scroll scenes — the pattern for rendering neighboring art windows through one shared canvas, with a camera and scissored viewport for each frame. MIT notice.
  • Codrops’ Magnetic Buttons — damped hover response, layered label movement, and rolling text. MIT notice.
  • Lenis 1.3.11 — smooth wheel scrolling synchronized with the animation clock. MIT notice.
  • Three.js physical materials and clearcoat example — reflective cobalt, brushed metal, and enamel materials.
  • Codrops: glass and plastic in Three.js — material and lighting research for the scene.

Libraries

Three.js, including its MIT-licensed RoomEnvironment and RoundedBoxGeometry, provides the renderer, lighting environment, and geometry. GSAP, ScrollTrigger, and SplitText handle entrances, heading reveals, interactive controls, and the project sequence.

The Lusion reference informed the visual direction; the public examples above informed specific implementations. This is not a claim about the libraries used by Lusion’s current site. No Lusion images, models, or production assets are reused. Motion can be paused, and small screens use a natural vertical layout.
